easy.def: A small stick with cotton on the end.
examples: The nurse used a swab.
A cotton swab is soft.
He used a swab.

more.def: A small piece of cotton or cloth on a stick, used for cleaning or putting on medicine.
examples: The nurse cleaned the cut with a cotton swab.
The doctor took a swab from my throat.
He used a swab to put medicine on the sore spot.

easy.def: To clean with a mop or cloth.
examples: The sailor swabs the deck.
She swabbed the floor.
He swabbed the cut.

more.def: To clean or wipe something with a mop or cloth.
examples: The sailors swabbed the deck of the ship.
She swabbed the floor with a wet mop.
The nurse swabbed the cut with a clean cloth.

easy.def: To walk in a proud, bold way.
examples: The rooster swaggered.
He swaggered across the room.
She swaggers like a king.

more.def: To walk or act in a way that shows you are very proud and sure of yourself.
examples: The rooster swaggered across the yard as if he owned the farm.
He swaggered onto the field after scoring the winning goal.
The pirate in the play swaggered across the stage.

easy.def: To make food go down your throat.
examples: I swallow my food.
She swallowed the pill.
The baby swallowed the milk.

more.def: To make food or drink go down your throat from your mouth.
examples: Chew your food well before you swallow.
The little boy swallowed his juice in one gulp.
The snake swallowed the egg whole.

easy.def: A small bird with a forked tail that flies fast.
examples: A swallow flew by.
The swallow built a nest.
Swallows fly fast.

more.def: A small, fast bird with long pointed wings and a forked tail.
examples: A swallow darted over the pond to catch insects.
Swallows build mud nests under bridges.
The swallows flew south for the winter.

easy.def: A wet, muddy land with many plants.
examples: Frogs live in the swamp.
The swamp is wet.
Alligators live in a swamp.

more.def: Low, wet land that is covered in water and full of plants and trees.
examples: Frogs croaked in the swamp at night.
The boat moved slowly through the swamp.
Alligators live in the swamps of the south.

easy.def: To trade one thing for another.
examples: We swap cards.
I swapped seats.
She swapped lunches.

more.def: To give something and get something else in its place.
examples: We swapped stickers at recess.
I swapped seats with my friend.
She swapped her apple for a cookie.

easy.def: A big group of insects flying together.
examples: A swarm of bees flew by.
We saw a swarm of flies.
The swarm landed on a tree.

more.def: A large group of insects, such as bees, moving together, or any big crowd moving along in one mass.
examples: A swarm of bees hung from the branch of the old apple tree.
The beekeeper moved the swarm into a new hive.
A swarm of children ran out of the school when the bell rang.

easy.def: To fly or move together in a big group.
examples: Bees swarm around the hive.
Kids swarmed the ice cream truck.
Ants swarmed over the cake.

more.def: To fly or move together in a large crowd, all at the same time.
examples: Ants swarmed over the dropped cookie within minutes.
Fans swarmed around the players after the big game.
Bees swarm out of the hive in the early spring.

easy.def: To hit something quickly with a flat hand or tool.
examples: I swat a fly.
She swatted the bug.
Dad swatted a mosquito.

more.def: To hit something sharply and quickly, especially an insect, with something flat.
examples: I swatted a fly that was buzzing around the kitchen.
She swatted the mosquito with a rolled-up newspaper.
The cat swatted at the toy that was dangling above her.

easy.def: To move slowly from side to side.
examples: The flowers sway in the wind.
The boat swayed.
I sway to the music.

more.def: To move slowly from one side to the other.
examples: The trees sway in the wind.
The boat swayed gently on the water.
She swayed to the music in her chair.

easy.def: To promise that you are telling the truth.
examples: I swear I did not eat it.
He swore to tell the truth.
She swears she saw a deer.

more.def: To make a serious promise that you are telling the truth or will do something.
examples: The witness swore to tell the truth.
I swear I will keep your secret.
He swore that he saw lights in the sky.

easy.def: To say rude words.
examples: Do not swear at school.
He swore when he dropped it.
Swearing is not polite.

more.def: To use rude or bad language.
examples: It is rude to swear in front of others.
He swore loudly when he stubbed his toe.
Many schools have a rule against swearing.

easy.def: Water that comes out of your skin when you are hot.
examples: Sweat ran down my face.
Sweat keeps you cool.
He wiped the sweat.

more.def: Salty water that comes out of the skin when you are hot or working hard.
examples: Sweat dripped from the runner's face.
Sweat helps your body cool down.
He wiped the sweat from his forehead.

easy.def: To have water come out of your skin.
examples: I sweat when I run.
He sweated in the sun.
Dogs do not sweat.

more.def: To give off salty water through the skin when you are hot.
examples: I sweat when I run on a hot day.
He sweated in the summer sun.
Runners sweat during a race.

easy.def: A warm top that you pull over your head.
examples: I wear a sweater.
The sweater is warm.
She knitted a sweater.

more.def: A warm piece of clothing, often knitted, that you wear over your shirt.
examples: I put on a sweater because it was cold.
Grandma knitted me a red sweater.
The sweater kept me warm.

easy.def: A soft, warm shirt with long sleeves.
examples: I wore a sweatshirt.
The sweatshirt is warm.
Her sweatshirt has a hood.

more.def: A soft, warm shirt with long sleeves, usually made of thick cotton, that people wear in cool weather or when exercising.
examples: I pulled on my sweatshirt because the evening was cool.
The team's sweatshirt had the school's name on the front.
She tied her sweatshirt around her waist when she got warm.

easy.def: Wet with sweat.
examples: My hands are sweaty.
I got sweaty at the game.
The sweaty shirt is in the wash.

more.def: Covered with sweat or wet from sweating.
examples: I was hot and sweaty after soccer practice.
My hands got sweaty before I went on stage.
He tossed his sweaty socks into the laundry basket.

easy.def: To clean with a broom.
examples: I sweep the floor.
Dad swept the porch.
Please sweep up the crumbs.

more.def: To clean a floor by brushing dirt away with a broom.
examples: I sweep the kitchen floor after dinner.
Dad swept the leaves off the porch.
She swept up the crumbs with a broom.

easy.def: Tasting like sugar.
examples: Honey is sweet.
The apple was sweet.
I like sweet cookies.

more.def: Having the taste of sugar or honey.
examples: Ripe strawberries are sweet and juicy.
The tea was too sweet for me.
Maple syrup is a sweet treat made from tree sap.

easy.def: Kind and nice.
examples: What a sweet kitten!
You are sweet to help me.
She gave me a sweet smile.

more.def: Kind, gentle and pleasant.
examples: It was sweet of you to share your lunch.
The baby has a sweet smile.
She wrote a sweet note to her teacher.

easy.def: A name for someone you love.
examples: Goodnight, sweetheart.
Thanks, sweetheart.
He called her sweetheart.

more.def: A loving name for someone you care about.
examples: "Time for bed, sweetheart," said Dad.
Grandma calls me sweetheart.
"Thank you, sweetheart; that was kind," said Grandpa.

easy.def: A loving name for a child or someone you like.
examples: Time for bed, sweetie.
Thank you, sweetie.
Come here, sweetie.

more.def: A loving name for a child or someone you care about.
examples: "Time for bed, sweetie," said Dad.
Grandma called me sweetie and gave me a hug.
"Thank you, sweetie," said the neighbor.

easy.def: In a kind, gentle or pleasing way.
examples: The baby smiled sweetly.
The bird sang sweetly.
She spoke sweetly.

more.def: In a gentle, kind or pleasing way, or with a sweet taste or sound.
examples: The baby smiled sweetly at everyone in the room.
The bird sang sweetly from the top of the tree.
The cake smelled sweetly of vanilla and sugar.

easy.def: The sweet taste of something.
examples: I love the sweetness of honey.
The cake had a lot of sweetness.
Taste the sweetness of the peach.

more.def: The quality of tasting like sugar, or of being kind and gentle.
examples: The sweetness of the ripe strawberries made everyone ask for more.
Lemon juice can balance the sweetness of a sugary drink.
Everyone loved the sweetness of her smile.

easy.def: To get bigger or fatter.
examples: My ankle will swell.
The river swelled.
The balloon swelled.

more.def: To grow bigger, rounder or fuller than normal.
examples: His ankle swelled after he twisted it.
The river swelled after days of heavy rain.
The sponge swells when it soaks up water.

easy.def: Very fast.
examples: The swift horse ran.
A swift river.
The cat was swift.

more.def: Moving or happening very fast.
examples: The swift horse ran across the field.
A swift river carried the leaf away.
The cat made a swift jump onto the table.

easy.def: Very quickly.
examples: The deer ran swiftly.
The river flows swiftly.
She swam swiftly.

more.def: In a fast way.
examples: The deer ran swiftly through the forest.
The river flowed swiftly after the rain.
She swam swiftly across the pool.

easy.def: To move through water using your body.
examples: Fish swim.
I swim in the pool.
We swam in the lake.

more.def: To move through water by using your arms, legs or fins.
examples: Fish swim with their fins.
She learned to swim at the pool.
We swam across the lake.

easy.def: A person who swims.
examples: She is a fast swimmer.
The swimmer dove.
A swimmer crossed the lake.

more.def: A person who swims, or an animal that swims.
examples: The lifeguard is a strong swimmer.
The swimmers dove into the pool.
A strong swimmer crossed the lake.

easy.def: Moving through water by moving your arms and legs.
examples: I love swimming.
Swimming is fun.
We go swimming in summer.

more.def: The sport or activity of moving through water by using your arms and legs.
examples: We go swimming at the lake in summer.
Swimming is good exercise.
She has swimming lessons on Saturdays.

easy.def: Pigs.
examples: The farmer raises swine.
The swine ate in the pen.
Swine live on the farm.

more.def: Pigs, or a pig; a word used mostly for farm animals.
examples: The farmer raises swine and chickens on his land.
A herd of swine rolled in the mud on a hot day.
The county fair had a contest for the best swine.

easy.def: A seat that hangs from ropes.
examples: I love the swing.
Push me on the swing.
The swing goes high.

more.def: A seat that hangs from ropes or chains and moves back and forth.
examples: The kids waited their turn on the swing.
Dad pushed me on the swing.
A rope swing hung from the tree.

easy.def: To move back and forth.
examples: The door swings.
I swing on the swing.
The monkey swings.

more.def: To move back and forth or in a curve while hanging.
examples: The monkey swung from branch to branch.
The door swung open in the wind.
She swung the bat and hit the ball.

easy.def: To move something across a surface in one quick motion.
examples: I swipe the screen.
She swiped her card.
He swiped his finger.

more.def: To move a finger or card quickly across something.
examples: I swipe the screen to see the next picture.
She swiped her card at the door.
He swiped his finger across the tablet.

easy.def: To hit at something with a fast swing.
examples: The cat swiped at the string.
He swiped at the fly.
The bear swiped at the bees.

more.def: To hit or reach at something with a fast sweeping movement.
examples: The cat swiped at the dangling string.
He swiped at the fly with his hand.
The bear swiped at the buzzing bees.

easy.def: A button that turns something on or off.
examples: Flip the light switch.
The switch is on the wall.
Turn the switch.

more.def: A small control that turns a machine or light on or off.
examples: Flip the switch to turn on the lamp.
The switch on the wall is broken.
He pressed the switch and the fan started.

easy.def: To change from one to another.
examples: Let us switch seats.
She switched hands.
I switched to blue.

more.def: To change from one thing to another.
examples: Let's switch seats so I can see.
She switched hands to hold the bag.
The team switched to a new plan.

easy.def: A weapon with a long, sharp blade.
examples: The knight held a sword.
The sword is sharp.
He drew his sword.

more.def: A weapon with a long metal blade and a handle.
examples: The knight held up his sword.
A sword hung on the castle wall.
Long ago, soldiers fought with swords.
